text:
Maya (CS): heads-up — drafting the post-incident follow-up for AcmeCorp/BrightApps about this morning's embeddings disruption (started ~09:12 UTC). Need confirmation on timeline and whether to offer a goodwill credit.

IncidentBot: Incident 2026-03-10-EMB-001 declared MAJOR. Pages triggered at 09:14 UTC. Mitigation began 09:22 UTC (automatic fallback). Capacity replaced and stabilized by 09:48 UTC; incident closed 10:05 UTC.

Eli (Oncall): short summary from oncall: a downstream deploy caused widespread KV cache invalidations, producing many cold starts. Autoscaler provision attempts hit provider 429 rate limits during retries which delayed new node availability. Automatic fallback to a quantized model lowered error rates but latency remained elevated until nodes joined.

Sahil (SRE): metrics/details: initial 5xx spike peaked around 1.1% then settled to 0.82% during fallback. Autoscaler requests began 09:13; cloud API returned 429s between ~09:14-09:21 across the affected regions. New instances passed health checks and joined at 09:46.

Maya (CS): Jordan requests a concise customer-facing downtime window to include in their internal RCA. Also: confirm if any customer data/PII was exposed in logs?

Sahil (SRE): confirmed: logs only contained internal request IDs, shard identifiers, and error codes. No customer content or PII. :white_check_mark:

Ava (Product): recommend including the exact error fraction (0.82%) in the customer note, and rephrase the timeline as "stabilized by 09:48 UTC; fully recovered by 10:05 UTC" for clarity.

Maya (CS): draft customer message below — please flag edits. Planning to propose one-month goodwill credit for affected routes and offer a 30-min technical review call.

--- DRAFT CUSTOMER NOTE ---
Hi team,

Thank you for your patience. On 2026-03-10 we experienced a brief degradation affecting the embeddings endpoint. Summary: 
- Impact window: ~09:12	10:05 UTC. Service stabilized by 09:48 UTC; full recovery verified at 10:05 UTC.
- Symptoms: elevated latency and a small portion of 5xx errors (0.82% of embeddings requests during the window).
- High-level cause: a cache invalidation following an internal deploy coincided with autoscaler retries being throttled by our cloud provider (HTTP 429s), delaying capacity provisioning and increasing cold starts.
- Data exposure: No customer PII or content was exposed.

Immediate mitigations and next steps:
- Immediate: automatic fallback to a quantized model reduced error rates while capacity provisioned.
- Short-term: revise autoscaler backoff/retry parameters and expand warm pool sizes for embeddings clusters.
- Long-term: implement regional warm pools, provider-rate-limit mitigations, and a synthetic warmup probe to detect cache churn preemptively.

We'd like to offer a goodwill credit equal to one month of usage for affected routes and a 30-minute technical review. Please let us know if you'd like to schedule time.

Regards,
Maya (Customer Success)
--- END DRAFT ---

Jordan (Account): Acme will want credit and a review. Ill prepare CSR-friendly wording and scheduling once Maya sends.

Maya (CS): Sahil, can you produce a short appendix timeline as bullets I can attach instead of pasting logs?

Sahil (SRE): Appendix timeline (bullets):
- 09:12 UTC: internal deploy triggered KV cache invalidations across embedding shards.
- 09:13 UTC: cold-start surge; autoscaler issued provisioning requests.
- 09:14 UTC: pages triggered; initial error spike observed.
- 09:15	10:21 UTC: autoscaler retries encountered cloud API 429s; repeated backoffs.
- 09:22 UTC: automatic fallback to model-quantized-1 activated for impacted routes.
- 09:30 UTC: error rate decreasing but latency remained elevated.
- 09:36 UTC: manual emergency scaling attempt; partial node acceptance.
- 09:46 UTC: new nodes registered and health-checks passed; cache warmups in progress.
- 09:48 UTC: system stabilized (errors near baseline; latency trending down).
- 10:05 UTC: incident closed after verification and monitoring watch.

Ava (Product): add ticket owners/ETAs for preventative work:
- FT-4212: autoscaler backoff & retry overhaul (owner: @Sahil) target 2026-03-24
- FT-4213: reserve warm pool + synthetic-warmup probe (owner: @InfraTeam) target 4 weeks
- FT-4214: provider-rate-limit mitigation & deploy preflight (owner: @Eli) target 6 weeks

Sahil (SRE): FT-4212 created with notes and ETA.

Eli (Oncall): I'll open infra ticket for regional warm pools and provider quota work; also propose a deploy preflight that simulates cache invalidation impact.

Maya (CS): can we send this to AcmeCorp in the next 30-45 minutes? I will attach the status page entry and the incident postmortem link when published.

Jordan (Account): send. I'll monitor replies and help schedule the review meeting: calendar.link/acmecorp-review

Maya (CS): proposed status page blurb: "2026-03-10  brief degradation impacting embeddings; mitigated via automatic fallback and capacity replacement. No customer data exposed. Full RCA to follow." Keep concise.

IncidentBot: Customer notification delivered to AcmeCorp at 11:03 UTC. Follow-up ticket created: TKT-2026-118.

Maya (CS): message sent. I'll update this thread when the postmortem and tickets are live. Thanks everyone. :pray:
